answer: Path-scarce routing tolls. Each new agent identity must route its first N transactions through a randomly assigned relay bridge; relay capacity is fixed and auctioned, so identities compete for the same scarce slots. Attackers pay rising auction prices per identity plus relay latency. Reputation accrues only after sustained valid traffic, like bees returning to an orchard. Honest agents recoup tolls via nectar rewards; sybils, lacking history, never do.
